output.brief:
Don't send the breach notice. The rise in Corvane's missed bags tracks the tag stock change on 1 September, not the handler change. Tags printed on the new Fennick stock fail automatic reading about 11.8% of the time, against about 1.5% on the old stock. The same counters failed only 1.6% on old stock in mid-October. Pelion, handled by the same Tessaly crews, stayed flat. Bags diverted to manual encoding rose from about 70 to about 455–470 a day. Encode wait times rose to about 30 minutes, and 91% of the encode-path bags that missed their flight reached the lateral after it closed. Bags that are read automatically are unchanged. The airport's reader equipment looks fine, and the added evening flights don't explain it.

I'm unsure whether the Fennick media is defective or the printer heat settings are wrong for it. Next steps: switch counters and kiosks back to the Brackwater stock held in stores, which should cover about five weeks. Then test the Fennick stock with the printer maker and supplier. Hold any defect claim against Fennick until that test is done. Consider a temporary extra encode workstation in the meantime. Review Tessaly's crew experience separately.
